newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold down on overseas sales pressure.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold down on overseas sales pressure.

text.p: Hong Kong gold ended Monday below New York's Friday close as the metal stayed under constant selling pressure from Japan and Australia, dealers said.
Bullion ended at US$343.70/344.20 an ounce on Monday against New York's US$344.50/345.00 close on Friday.
Selling from traders on the Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM) and from Australian producers kept up the pressure on Monday, dealers said.
Erratic performance kept dealers warily away from the market, gold sources said.
"Gold performed pretty well on Friday and it's been under constant pressure today so people are standing aside," a bullion dealer at an international bank said.
Some described market sentiment as "confused" as traders debated whether Friday's optimistic performance had been a fluke or part of a steady trend up.
Dealers saw resistence at $347 per ounce, with $349 per ounce the cap.
"The market has been moving over a wide range (recently), up to two or three dollars," said a trader at a local bullion firm.
Physical gold demand was seen healthy as traders gradually returned to their desks from a lengthy Chinese New Year break, some sources said.
With New York closed Monday for the U.S. President's Day holiday, trade would simmer on a low flame, dealers said.
Local gold ended HK$13 lower at HK$3,190 a tael. The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society remained at +8.00, unchanged from its Saturday fix.
Some bullion traders said that players held long and short positions at the exchange and that the longs were seeking to push interest rates up to receive interest.
